entries.english: June 1260, Hohenfurt. Wok von Rosenberg, marshal of Bohemia, makes known that, with the consent and express will of his wife and all his relatives on both sides, and by divine inspiration, he has granted in perpetuity to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt, which he has begun to found and build in honor of the Blessed Virgin Mary for the salvation of his soul and those of his ancestors and successors, the lands and revenues listed below, with full rights and defined boundaries. The property includes woodland and meadows by the Wulta and its streams, extending to Helfenberg, the Bohemian-Bavarian forest boundary, and the lands of Witigo of Krum(l)au; fishing rights in the Wulta from the meadow of Zbyadel to Witigo’s boundary, though Wok’s own fishermen may also fish there; churches and shares of tithes, villages, farms, and other revenues listed in the charter. The grant includes, among other things, the church at Rosental with all its use and a third of the tithes from Wok’s villages and others granted in fief. The charter was sealed. Witnesses included the brothers Heinrich and Werenhard von Schowenberg, younger brothers Werenhard and Heinrich of the same house, Budewoy and his brother Witigo von Krum(l)au, Poppo, Johannes, Gerbert, and Benata and Benisius, burgraves of Rosenberg, among others. Done at Hohenfurt and written at Rosenberg in June 1260. The seal, formerly on red silk, is now entirely crumbled.
